geometry.summary: A vertical column from the soles through the pelvis and ribcage to the crown, with a base triangle formed by the two feet and the pelvic floor. Feet hip-width or together; legs long without locked knees; arms soft at the sides; spine stacked in one clear upright line.
geometry.svg_hint: line from midfeet through pelvis to crown; base triangle feet-to-pelvic-floor

reaction.name: Settle
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: attention that was bouncing outward settles into quiet vertical presence. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.cue: Even inhale four, even exhale four. No forced hold. Notice the natural brief turn at the top and bottom of each breath.

orientation.cue: Crown over heels; weight even on both feet
orientation.gravity: Down through the triple foot points (heel, big-toe ball, little-toe ball); up through the crown
orientation.gaze: Soft horizontal, eyes open or lightly closed
orientation.degrees_hint: 0 degrees tilt from vertical; no lean forward or back

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Exhalation rises and inhalation descends as a continuous emission. Rest awareness at the two places where these flows arise or turn; fullness (bharita) becomes available.
adiyogi.method_summary: In standing stillness, follow natural breath without forcing. At the end of inhale and the end of exhale, rest attention for a moment in the brief turn (inner center and outer dvadasanta as classical map). Do not strain or stop the breath; notice the pause that is already there.

honesty.disclosure: This asana and VBT method are linked by the School of 112 Doorways as a teaching device (Door 001 with dharana 001). It is not a claim of ancient one-to-one canon.
honesty.notes: Supportive resonance only: Tadasana stillness makes the two breath-turn points easier to notice. Pairing remains school_device by door index.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: If standing is not available, practice the same breath-turn attention seated upright in an open seat (sukhasana or chair).
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Soften the knees if locking bothers them. Sit or hold a wall if balance or fatigue appear.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 001, Mountain — Tadasana. Stand as a quiet upright column. Nothing to prove. Just arrive.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: Feet plant. Legs long, knees soft. Pelvis stacked over ankles, ribs over pelvis, crown floating up. Arms rest by your sides. One vertical line.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Crown over heels. Weight even on both feet — heel, big-toe ball, little-toe ball. Gaze soft and level. Gravity down, length up.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Inhale for four. Exhale for four. Six easy cycles. Breath lands in the lower belly, then soft ribs. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Hold the soles-to-crown line. Secondary: notice the natural turn at the top of the inhale and the bottom of the exhale.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: Name the school shift Settle: scattered charge moves toward grounded stillness. Feel it as metaphor, not medicine.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: From VBT dharana 001: rest awareness at the two places where breath turns. Do not stop the breath. Meet the pause that is already there.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Take one free breath. Soften the knees. Carry the vertical quiet into the next step, or sit if you need rest.
